result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A centres the whole screen on one action, booking a first wheel session, and keeps everything else to two short rules. It also says plainly that bookings appear on the dashboard and can be moved or cancelled. B is polished and uses rich studio wording, but its first visible step is a 10-minute orientation that competes with booking, and its studio info panel (membership, kiln dates, tech on shift) adds clutter. A loses a little on rubric item 5 because its 'Book this session' button shows greyed out until a time is picked and it labels its data 'SAMPLE STUDIO', which looks placeholder-like. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B makes booking a first wheel session the clear headline task. It shows concrete time slots, says what happens next (the booking appears on your dashboard, where you can move or cancel it), and keeps the side info to two short rules. A has warm studio-specific copy and a useful 'cancel free up to 12 hours ahead' line, but its main action is step 3 of a checklist. That step competes with an orientation task and a busy studio-info sidebar, so the next step is less obvious.
